blocks.intro: In McHenry, a lot of faucet trouble starts with the water:

tiles.h3: Scale Around the Spout and Handles
tiles.body: Hard water leaves white crust that eats into finishes and works into the moving parts.
Mineral buildup on the cartridge or seals keeps them from closing fully.
A scaled-up aerator or cartridge. Cleaning or replacing it usually fixes it.
Loose supply lines or a corroded shutoff valve.

bodies: We repair dripping, stiff and leaking kitchen faucets and install new ones, including pull-downs, touchless models and taps for drinking water filters. In hard water, a faucet with ceramic disc cartridges and a finish that resists spotting lasts longer.
During every install, we check the shutoff valves and supply lines under the sink. Valves scaled by hard water often won't close fully. We replace them while the sink is open.
We handle sink drains, dishwasher connections, refrigerator and ice maker lines, disposals and gas hookups for ranges, plus new layouts for remodels.

Sink clogged? See [drain cleaning](/mchenry/drain-cleaning). Disposal not working? See [garbage disposal repair](/mchenry/garbage-disposal-installation-repair). Want filtered drinking water at the sink? See [water filtration](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems).

img.alt: Plumbing under a double kitchen sink: white PVC drain and P-trap, braided supply lines with chrome shutoff valves, and a garbage disposal

bodies: We install sinks, faucets, toilets, showerheads, tub fillers, laundry tubs and outdoor spigots, from one swap to a full bathroom. Each install includes connections, new shutoffs where needed and a leak check.

Buying your own fixtures? Send us the make and model and we'll confirm the fit. For toilets, see [toilet installation](/mchenry/toilet-installation-repair). For showers, see [shower repair](/mchenry/shower-repair).

blocks.h2: Faucets and Fixtures in McHenry Homes
blocks.intro: Hard water and homes built mostly since 1970 shape fixture work here.

items.body: Mineral buildup wears cartridges and seals faster. A softener upstream protects every new fixture you install.
In homes from the 1990s and 2000s, all the faucets tend to wear out together. Replacing several in one visit saves a trip.
If your fixtures show orange stains, the water may carry iron. A [water test](/mchenry/water-filtration-systems) tells you.

blocks.h2: Faucet and Fixture Questions From McHenry Homeowners

items.q: How do I get scale off my faucets?
items.preview: Soak the aerator in vinegar. Heavy scale may mean replacing parts.
items.answer: Unscrew the aerator and soak it in white vinegar to dissolve the scale. Wipe fixtures regularly. If scale has worked into the cartridge, replacing it is the fix. A softener prevents most of it.

items.q: Why does my new faucet already have weak flow?
items.preview: Scale or debris in the aerator, or old supply lines.
items.answer: Often debris or scale from the pipes collects in the new aerator. Rinse it. If that doesn't help, the supply line or valve may be restricted.

items.q: Can you install a drinking water faucet?
items.answer: Yes. We install dedicated drinking water faucets with under-sink filters or reverse osmosis systems.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my faucet?
items.preview: Repair a good faucet with a worn part. Replace a corroded one.
items.answer: If it's a quality faucet with a worn cartridge, repair it. If the finish is failing or scale has damaged the body, replace it.

items.q: How much does faucet installation cost in McHenry?
items.preview: It depends on the faucet and valves. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the faucet, the condition of the shutoffs and supply lines and access. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
